thread:
maria (People Ops): quick follow-up from today's all-hands on reviews/comp. dropping clarifications here + links. please add Qs.

maria (People Ops): timeline summary: kickoff May 10 -> self-reviews due May 24 -> calibration Jun 1-7 -> notifications Jun 21. see full guide: https://redwood.example.com/hr/reviews-2026

tasha (IC): If I'm on a performance plan, can I still be considered for a raise/promo this cycle?

maria (People Ops): yes, in some cases. Performance improvement plans don't automatically disqualify someone, but managers must include remediation progress and a recommendation in calibration. Deviations will be handled case-by-case.

devin (Manager): For calibration notes, is there a preferred template? saves us from back-and-forth.

maria (People Ops): please use the 'Calibration Note' template on the review doc (link above). Key: 3 bullet impact examples, peer feedback summary, and a proposed band + comp ask if any.

oliver (VP Eng): adding: for engineers, include quantifiable impact where possible (latency improvements, revenue-sourced metrics, active users affected).

lin (CTO): For early-career hires (<6mo), exceptions are rare. If your hire rapidly ramped and led a cross-team deliverable, include evidence and we'll flag for accelerated review.

tasha (IC): How do mid-cycle market comps work? I heard there's a pool.

peopleops-bot: market-adjustment-policy: https://redwood.example.com/hr/market-adjusts-2026. Short: small mid-cycle pool for retention risk and critical roles. Submit via CompChange form.

maria (People Ops): mid-cycle requests need manager justification + director signoff. We triage by retention risk and replacement cost.

devin (Manager): If a manager requests an off-cycle comp change and it gets approved after calibration but before notifications, do we update the notification letter?

maria (People Ops): yes — we update offer/notification letters with final comp. final comp in HR system is authoritative.

tasha (IC): Promo timing question: if promoted, when is equity grant issued?

peopleops-bot: equity-refresh cadence: typical grant run in late June post-notifications; timing dependent on board approvals.

maria (People Ops): promoted folks are prioritized for the June grant batch but not guaranteed. we'll communicate specifics in the notification email.

oliver (VP Eng): managers: please avoid vague language in notes like "exceptional". Cite specific outcomes, timelines, and stakeholder impact.

tasha (IC): Is there guidance for leveling between IC3 and IC4? examples would help.

maria (People Ops): we'll drop a short leveling rubric in #people-ops by EOD tomorrow with examples of scope, autonomy, and influence per band.

lin (CTO): also planning a 30-min calibration office hours next Wed for managers who want live feedback on notes.

devin (Manager): If someone has compensation sensitive info (offer outside the company) — how should we surface that in calibration?

maria (People Ops): include it as manager note and mark as "confidential" in the calibration form. HR will treat it confidentially during review.

peopleops-bot: Quick poll: Do you want a manager-only calibration template walkthrough?

	Yes 	 9
	No 	 3

maria (People Ops): thanks all. we'll post the rubric + template link in channel and schedule the office hours. if you need 1:1 help drafting calibration notes, DM me. :calendar: :white_check_mark:

peopleops-bot: Thread closed for new top-level questions at EOD; replies still ok.
